title: Token flow from Sky to a Prime stops the moment the Prime begins generating income
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.7.3 makes the cutover automatic: "Upon the commencement of Income Generation... by a Prime, any existing or previously agreed-upon allocation or distribution of MKR or SKY tokens from Sky to that Prime shall immediately cease. The intent is for the Primes to transition to financial self-sufficiency upon the initiation of their respective income-generating activities."

Tying subsidy termination to a *capability* trigger rather than a date is the substantive choice. A dated cliff can arrive before a Prime is viable or long after; conditioning on income generation means support ends exactly when it stops being necessary, and no renegotiation is required to end it. Since Income Generation is itself deemed to commence on July 1, 2025, the trigger is also unambiguous in practice.

The section then adds pressure toward the TGE from a second direction: "any token vesting to the Prime Foundation will be reduced by 50% until the TGE occurs." A Prime that delays its token event therefore faces the 30% income penalty, the 70% income credit and halved Foundation vesting simultaneously — three independent costs all pointing at the same milestone.

The final requirement reaches inside the Prime's own compensation design: "Prior to the TGE, Primes agree to share with Sky the Prime Agent Token vesting schedules and lock-ups for their teams to ensure they align with the principles of long-term commitment to the Prime."

That is a disclosure obligation about a Prime's internal arrangements, justified on alignment grounds. It fits the wider pattern in this Accord — Sky holds most of the token supply, retains a universal override over it, and reviews how the remainder is distributed to the people building the protocol.
description: Any existing or agreed MKR or SKY allocation ceases immediately on Income Generation, and Foundation token vesting is cut by half until the TGE occurs, with team vesting schedules shared with Sky.
